purpose: The eight community samples the package-follow probe carries across every base hop (task 20261118-01, D3). One row per sample: what to install, where its fake config and data marker live, and the single command that decides whether it is still USABLE - not merely still recorded as installed.
check_contract: check.cmd runs on the machine, prints one line of fact=value fields; check.expect is the POSIX ERE that line has to match. The driver compares the two and has no per-package branch, so every criterion is reviewed here rather than read out of a shell nest. The remote preamble defines the helpers a command may use: _ver <pkg> (installed version or empty), _missing <pkg> (payload files the package record names but disk no longer has, etc/uci-defaults excluded because the base consumes those at first boot), _http <path> (status code from the machine's own web server over loopback), _svc <init> <proc> (running|stopped|expected-not-running|missing, without starting anything), _bin <init> <name> (the daemon path the init script's own PROG names, else the one PATH resolves; never a hard-coded directory, because the directory is not the same on every base), _sha <path>. setup, when present, runs on the machine during --install, after apk add succeeds and before --mark records the baseline: it is the only place a sample may change the machine's running state, and the install row carries setup=ok|failed|skipped|absent so a setup that did not run is visible rather than implied.
ready_contract: ready, when present, says the criterion cannot answer until a daemon is up, and that the machine may still be about to start it. ready.proc is the process the daemon runs as and ready.init is its init script; either one saying the service runs counts as 'up'. ready.settle is the line the running boot appends to its ring log once it has finished restarting the daemons procd gave up on - on this product that is stage=services-reconciled, written by ab-boot's detached follow worker after the first boot's package follow has settled, which measured an uptime of about 120 s on the reference machine. Until that line exists a daemon that is down is not yet a failed one. ready.timeout (seconds) and ready.interval (seconds) bound the wait: a sample whose daemon never comes up is reported as a failure with the seconds it waited and what the machine last said, never as a pass and never as an unbounded wait. A sample without ready is asked once, exactly as before.

samples.name: luci-theme-argon
samples.why: The theme's own stylesheet served by this base's uhttpd: a package whose files survived but whose static tree no longer resolves (or whose menu.d/ucode view stopped loading) answers something other than 200. 'apk list --installed' would still say installed, which is exactly the difference this criterion is here to see. The design fixed this path as the theme criterion.
samples.limits: It proves the web path serves the theme asset, not that a browser renders it: no JavaScript is executed.

samples.name: luci-app-argon-config

check.cmd: r=$(/usr/libexec/rpcd/luci.argon list 2>/dev/null | head -c 200); case "$r" in *remove*) rpc=ok ;; *) rpc=bad ;; esac; j=$(_http /luci-static/resources/view/argon-config.js); m=$(_missing luci-app-argon-config); echo "rpc=$rpc js=${j:-none} missing=$m"

samples.why: The theme's config page is a ucode rpcd plugin plus a JS view. Executing the plugin's 'list' method proves the ucode/ubus ABI still runs on this base (a base hop that changes ucode or rpcd breaks it while the package record stays intact), and the 200 on its view proves the page asset is still served. Measured on the reference machine 2026-11-18: the plugin answers { "remove": ..., "rename": ... }.
samples.limits: It does not drive the page in a browser; the ACL/rpcd session path is exercised by luci-entry-probe.

samples.name: luci-app-openclash

check.cmd: e=no; [ -x /etc/init.d/openclash ] && sh -n /etc/init.d/openclash 2>/dev/null && e=yes; s=$(_svc /etc/init.d/openclash clash); m=$(_missing luci-app-openclash); echo "init=$e svc=$s missing=$m"

samples.why: A proxy app is broken in the ways this criterion sees: its init entry gone or no longer parsable by this base's shell, or its payload partly missing after the overlay merge. All three service states a non-started daemon can be in are accepted, because the probe deliberately does not start a proxy (see limits): 'expected-not-running' is what the package measures as on the reference machine 2026-11-19 without any hop, so treating it as broken made a steady state read as a regression and took five matrix cases with it. What separates the states is the baseline, not this ERE: the driver records the criterion's output at --mark, so a sample whose init or payload was sound before the hop and is not after it still fails, while a criterion that never matched before the hop is reported as a gap and named. Measured on the reference machine 2026-11-18: luci-app-openclash is in the luci feed and /dev/net/tun is absent until kmod-tun is installed, so the tun device is reported as a fact by the install step instead of being asserted here.
samples.limits: It does not start OpenClash: a start rewrites nftables and the machine's routing, which is not a probe's decision to make on a shared device. For the same reason a proxy that ran and then stopped is not visible here - the probe never made it run - so the row's meaning is 'the package's init, payload and boot enablement survived', not 'the tunnel is up'.

samples.name: luci-app-ttyd

check.cmd: e=no; [ -x /etc/init.d/ttyd ] && sh -n /etc/init.d/ttyd 2>/dev/null && e=yes; b=$(_bin /etc/init.d/ttyd ttyd); s=$(_svc /etc/init.d/ttyd ttyd); m=$(_missing luci-app-ttyd); echo "init=$e bin=${b:-none} svc=$s missing=$m"

samples.why: The official-feed control sample: it distinguishes 'the community package broke' from 'the whole feed/base broke'. Its init script must parse under the running base's shell, its daemon binary must still be there, its payload must be complete, and a service enabled at boot must actually run - the last one is the only state that separates 'installed' from 'works' for a daemon sample. The binary is looked up through _bin, which asks the init script's own PROG and then PATH, and the row prints the path it found: the first version of this criterion hard-coded /usr/sbin/ttyd and failed a healthy machine, because on this image /etc/init.d/ttyd:8 sets PROG=/usr/bin/ttyd (measured 2026-11-19). The path stays a fact in the row rather than disappearing into a yes/no, so a base that moves the binary is visible in the row that judged it. config_path is /etc/config/ttyd and not /etc/config/luci-app-ttyd, which is the same mistake one step further in: the sample is named after the LuCI app, but the file the daemon reads is the one its own init script loads - /etc/init.d/ttyd runs config_load "$NAME" with NAME=ttyd - and luci-app-ttyd ships no /etc/config file at all (measured 2026-11-19: apk info -L lists usr/share/luci/menu.d, usr/share/rpcd/acl.d and two JS views, nothing under etc/config). A marker written to /etc/config/luci-app-ttyd went to a file nothing reads, so the row proved nothing about the configuration the daemon actually starts with, while the file that does matter was left unmeasured.
samples.limits: Like OpenClash it does not start the daemon; the running-branch only applies to a machine where ttyd is already enabled. The fake config it marks is a `config marker 'ab_follow'` section appended to the file --mark found, and the init script starts an instance per section of type ttyd only (config_foreach validate_section_ttyd ttyd), so the marker is invisible to the daemon: measured 2026-11-19, ttyd starts with the marker in /etc/config/ttyd and the service is running, which is why this sample's fake config cannot be what stops the daemon.

samples.name: istore

check.cmd: v=$(_ver istore); f=$(ls /usr/libexec/istore* 2>/dev/null | head -1); echo "ver=${v:-none} launcher=${f:-none}"

samples.why: The software-store class. Round 03 measured apk add istore rc=1 on this feed line ('istore (no such package)', re-measured 2026-11-18), so this sample is expected to be a named GAP and never a FAIL: a sample the feed does not offer says nothing about the A/B machinery. When a machine does have it, the criterion is its launcher and an apk record, which is the whole of what the design asks for this class.
samples.limits: It cannot distinguish a store whose launcher is present from one whose LuCI page is broken; the page belongs to the store's own packaging, not to this project.

samples.name: docker

check.cmd: c=no; docker -v >/dev/null 2>&1 && c=yes; d=no; docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && d=yes; echo "client=$c daemon=$d"

samples.why: The kernel-facing sample: 'docker info' only answers when the client, the daemon and the kernel features the daemon needs (overlay2, cgroups, iptables) all agree on this base, so it fails for exactly the case this task exists for - a package that follows to a new kernel without its ABI following with it. That answer needs a running daemon, so this is the one sample with a setup: --install runs it after apk add, and the enable half is what makes the daemon come back on its own after every hop (a hop reboots the machine; a daemon that was only started once would be gone at the next --verify). The install row carries setup=ok|failed|skipped|absent, so a setup that did not run is a fact in the report rather than an assumption. It is also the one sample with a ready block, because the daemon is not up when the hop's ssh answers: the first boot of a new base follows packages in a detached worker and only then restarts the daemons procd gave up on (measured 2026-11-19: stage=services-reconciled started=1 down=dockerd, at an uptime of about 120 s, while the probe asked at about 25 s). Without the wait the criterion answers 'client=yes daemon=no' on a healthy machine, which is what turned six matrix cases red in round 5.
samples.limits: The daemon is started on the machine, which is a change of running state that only --install makes and that --unmark does not undo: an operator who wants the machine quiet again stops dockerd by hand. A setup that fails (for instance dockerd cannot start on this base) makes the install row a GAP: the sample cannot be carried, and the row says so instead of reporting a green daemon that never existed. The wait bounds the readiness question but does not answer it: a daemon that never comes up within ready.timeout is a FAIL carrying waited=<n>s and daemon=<starting|booting|down>, so a slow start and a broken package stay distinguishable in the row rather than collapsing into one 'not usable'.

samples.name: kmod-usb-storage

check.cmd: k=$(uname -r); ko=$(ls /lib/modules/$k/usb-storage.ko* 2>/dev/null | head -1); p=no; [ -n "$ko" ] && p=ko; grep -q usb-storage.ko /lib/modules/$k/modules.builtin 2>/dev/null && p=builtin; if [ "$p" = no ] && [ -d /sys/module/usb_storage ]; then p=sysfs; fi; l=no; grep -qE '^usb[-_]storage' /proc/modules && l=yes; m=$(_missing kmod-usb-storage); echo "kernel=$k mod=$p loaded=$l missing=$m"

samples.why: The ABI sample: a kmod is built for one kernel, so the module has to exist for the RUNNING kernel - as a .ko under /lib/modules/$(uname -r), or as a built-in this kernel was compiled with. A hop that swaps the kernel leaves the package record saying installed while the payload names the old kernel's paths, which is the case this criterion separates from health. Measured on the reference machine (25.12.2, 6.12.103, 2026-11-18): usb-storage is built in - /lib/modules/6.12.103/modules.builtin names kernel/drivers/usb/storage/usb-storage.ko and the package ships only /etc/modules.d/usb-storage - so a criterion that looked for the .ko alone would report a healthy sample as broken. 'loaded' is reported, not asserted: the module loads when a USB disk appears and the reference machine has none.
samples.limits: It does not modprobe the module: loading one is a device state change, so /proc/modules and the kernel's own builtin list are read instead.

samples.name: htop

check.cmd: htop --version >/dev/null 2>&1; r=$?; v=$(_ver htop); echo "rc=$r ver=${v:-none}"

samples.why: The pure user-space control: no kernel dependency and no daemon, so a red htop row means the base's libc/loader stopped running an old binary - the plainest form of 'the package is there but no longer usable'.
samples.limits: It proves the binary starts and prints its version, not that it draws a screen.
